Confusable pairs among the alcohol limits and penalties, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in trailing lines.

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A01
The per se DWI limit is 0.08 for an ordinary driver but 0.04 for a driver of a commercial motor vehicle. [A01]
Why it matters: group limits; difficulty medium; confusable regular versus commercial limit.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A01
The 0.05 figure is where crash risk starts to rise, not a legal limit; the legal per se limit for a car driver is 0.08. [A01]
Why it matters: group limits; confusable risk level versus legal limit.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A01
Refusing the chemical test brings at least 30 days of immediate revocation plus at least 12 months from DMV, while failing it at 0.08 or more brings an immediate revocation of at least 30 days. [A01]
Why it matters: group revocations; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A02
The restored-license BAC restriction is 0.04 the first time and 0.00 for every later restoration. [A02]
Why it matters: group restrictions; confusable with the commercial per se limit of the same value.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A02
The ignition interlock is triggered by a BAC of 0.15 or more or a prior conviction within seven years, while a fourth conviction becomes a felony when three priors fall within seven years. [A02]
Why it matters: group penalties; confusable seven-year windows.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A02
Look-back windows differ by conviction: three years for the four-year second-offense revocation, five years for permanent revocation on a third, seven years for the felony fourth. [A02]
Why it matters: group penalties; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A03
A driver younger than twenty-one who is convicted of driving with any amount of alcohol or drugs in their body faces a one-year driver license revocation [A03].
Why it matters: group underage; prereq graduated licensing provisional rule.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A03
An adult who lends an ID to an underage buyer or gives alcohol to an underage person faces the same one-year revocation as the underage buyer. [A03]
Why it matters: group underage; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A01
An open container is banned anywhere in a car's passenger area, while in a commercial vehicle's passenger area even closed containers are banned. [A01]
Why it matters: group containers; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]
